newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe expands China offshore effort.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe expands China offshore effort.

text.p: Santa Fe Energy Resources Inc said Thursday it has signed two production sharing contracts with the China National Offshore Oil Co giving Santa Fe Energy the right to explore in two areas of the South China Sea.

The company said it holds 100 percent of the working interest in both contract areas and has committed to programs of seismic reprocessing, acquisition of additional seismic data and drilling in each of the two blocks.
Block 15/34 covers an area of some 800,000 acres in the Pearl River Mouth Basin, China's largest offshore producing region, located about 50 miles south of Hong Kong.
It adjoins Block 27/11, where Santa Fe Energy previously acquired a 40 percent interest in an area operated by Kerr-McGee Corp.

The second contract area, Block 23/28, is located north of the large island of Hainan and covers an area of nearly half a million acres in the southern portion of the Beibu Gulf Basin. Its geology is very similar to the northern part of the Beibu Gulf Basin where multiple discoveries have been made. The area is also geologically similar to the Pearl River Mouth Basin and resembles portions of western Indonesia where Santa Fe has recently been successful.
